Contesto: Liferay 7.4 (portal-7.4-ga30), Java 11, OSGi. Devo esporre un HttpServlet OSGi (service = javax.servlet.Servlet) raggiungibile all'URL `/o/role-switch/toggle`.

Ho due servlet OSGi nello stesso runtime, entrambi registrati con proprietà del componente:
- servlet A: `osgi.http.whiteboard.context.path=/verificaEmail`, `osgi.http.whiteboard.servlet.pattern=/*`
- servlet B: `osgi.http.whiteboard.context.path=/role-switch`, `osgi.http.whiteboard.servlet.pattern=/*`

Sintomo osservato: una GET a `/o/role-switch/toggle` viene servita dal servlet A (verificaEmail), non dal servlet B. Il servlet B non riceve mai la richiesta.

Domande precise, rispondi con riferimenti alla documentazione ufficiale Liferay 7.4 e/o alla OSGi HTTP Whiteboard Specification (R7):

1. La proprietà `osgi.http.whiteboard.context.path` è valida su un componente SERVLET, oppure appartiene esclusivamente a un servizio `ServletContextHelper`? Cosa succede se la si mette su un servlet (viene ignorata? crea un context implicito)?

2. Due servlet registrati con lo stesso pattern `/*` sullo stesso ServletContextHelper: come si risolve il conflitto? (service.ranking, service.id, shadowing). Viene loggato un errore/warning?

3. Qual è il modo CORRETTO e idiomatico in Liferay 7.4 per esporre un servlet OSGi su un path dedicato tipo `/o/role-switch/*`? Mostra le proprietà esatte del @Component. In particolare:
   - basta usare `osgi.http.whiteboard.servlet.pattern=/role-switch/*` sul context di default? In tal caso l'URL finale è `/o/role-switch/...`?
   - oppure serve registrare un `ServletContextHelper` dedicato con `osgi.http.whiteboard.context.name` + `osgi.http.whiteboard.context.path` e poi sul servlet `osgi.http.whiteboard.context.select=(osgi.http.whiteboard.context.name=...)`?

4. Con il context di default Liferay (`/o`), un pattern specifico `/role-switch/*` ha precedenza su un pattern `/*` di un altro servlet (regola "most specific wins" della servlet spec)? Così il servlet B verrebbe correttamente invocato per `/o/role-switch/toggle` anche se il servlet A resta su `/*`?

Mi serve la configurazione @Component minima e corretta per garantire che `/o/role-switch/toggle` arrivi al MIO servlet, senza dipendere dall'ordine di registrazione.

## OSGi Servlet Whiteboard Pattern

Servlets are registered with one or more pattern through the osgi.http.whiteboard.servlet.pattern service property.

## Key Properties

At least one of the following properties must be specified on Servlet Whiteboard services: osgi.http.whiteboard.servlet.pattern, osgi.http.whiteboard.servlet.name, or osgi.http.whiteboard.servlet.errorPage.

## Context Selection

If multiple Servlet Context Helper services match the osgi.http.whiteboard.context.select property the servlet, filter, resource or listener will be registered with all these Servlet Context Helpers.

## Liferay Implementation Example

Here's a practical example from Liferay documentation: A servlet can be configured with properties like "osgi.http.whiteboard.context.path=/", "osgi.http.whiteboard.servlet.name=my.package.name.myTest", and "osgi.http.whiteboard.servlet.pattern=/myTest/test", with the servlet URL being http://localhost:8080/o/myTest/test.

Liferay uses the OSGi HTTP Whiteboard service for exposing all servlets, filters, etc.

The `/o/` path prefix you mentioned appears to be Liferay's convention for OSGi-based servlet endpoints in the portal URL structure.

I've successfully found comprehensive information about the OSGi HTTP Whiteboard Specification R7 regarding servlet context paths and ServletContextHelper. Here are the key findings:

## ServletContextHelper Overview

A ServletContextHelper is a helper service for a servlet context used by a Http Whiteboard implementation to serve HTTP requests, defining methods that the Http Whiteboard implementation may call to get information for a request when dealing with whiteboard services.

## Context Path Configuration

A context is registered with the "osgi.http.whiteboard.context.path" service property to define a path under which all services registered with this context are reachable. More specifically, the value is either a slash for the root or it must start with a slash but not end with a slash, with valid characters defined in rfc3986#section-3.3, and contexts with an invalid path are ignored.

## Context Naming and Registration

Each ServletContextHelper is registered with a "osgi.http.whiteboard.context.name" service property containing a name to reference by servlets, servlet filters, resources, and listeners. If there is more than one ServletContextHelper registered with the same context name, the one with the highest service ranking is active, the others are inactive.

## Service Association

Servlets, servlet filters, resources, and listeners services may be associated with a ServletContextHelper service with the "osgi.http.whiteboard.context.select" service property, and if the referenced ServletContextHelper service does not exist or is currently not active, the whiteboard services for that ServletContextHelper are not active either.

The official OSGi documentation provides extensive details at the [OSGi Compendium 7 HTTP Whiteboard Specification](https://docs.osgi.org/specification/osgi.cmpn/7.0.0/service.http.whiteboard.html).

content.content:
# OSGi Http Whiteboard Properties & Servlet Registration

## 1) osgi.http.whiteboard.context.path Validity

**osgi.http.whiteboard.context.path is ONLY valid on ServletContextHelper services**, not on Servlet services.

According to Table 140.1, this property is required for `ServletContextHelper` registration to define the "Additional prefix to the context path for servlets."

If incorrectly placed on a servlet service, the Http Whiteboard implementation would ignore it since the property is not listed in Table 140.4 (Servlet service properties). The servlet would still be registered using only the valid properties it possesses.

## 2) Servlet Pattern Conflict Resolution

When two servlets share identical patterns on the same context, conflicts resolve through **service ranking hierarchy**:

"Servlet and resource service registrations associated with a single Servlet Context share the same namespace. In case of identical registration patterns, service ranking rules are used to select the service handling a request."

The winning servlet becomes active; the shadowed servlet appears in failure DTOs. If service rankings tie, the lowest service ID wins (standard OSGi comparison). The specification explicitly notes that "The above rules can cause servlets that are already bound becoming unbound if a better match arrives," ensuring predictable outcomes regardless of registration order.

## 3) Servlet Context Matching Rules

URL dispatch follows a **longest-path-first principle** across contexts:

"The Servlet Context Helper service with the longest matching path is matched first. In the case of two Servlet Context Helpers with the same path, the service with the highest ranking is searched first."

Whole path segments must match exactly—`/foo/bars` cannot partially match `/foo/bar`.

## 4) Correct Servlet Registration at Dedicated Context Path

Register a custom `ServletContextHelper` with your desired path, then associate the servlet:

```
@HttpWhiteboardContext(name = "my-context", path = "/myapp")
// Register ServletContextHelper

@HttpWhiteboardServletPattern("/myservlet")
@HttpWhiteboardContextSelect("(osgi.http.whiteboard.context.name=my-context)")
// Register servlet
```

The servlet becomes accessible at the combined path: `/myapp/myservlet`.
